_comment: Workflows created automatically with each new catalog.
'script' is the identity key: workflow_triggers.py resolves chains by script
basename, and a workflow that is not registered for a catalog is silently
skipped. A typo here produces a workflow that runs when clicked and is never
part of any chain, with no error anywhere.
'order' is display order only. Execution order comes from DEPENDS_ON in
workflow_triggers.py and is unaffected by row ids.
This file lives in workflows/ because that directory is bind-mounted into
the backend container: it can be edited without rebuilding the image, and it
is read fresh on each use rather than cached at import.

workflows.name: Legacy Two-Stage Import
workflows.description: The previous import, kept while the streaming import (Ingest Files) proves itself: the same result, one stage after another. Import photos and videos from the source directory, extract EXIF, and create browser-friendly versions.
_default_comment: NOT seeded with a new catalog, unlike everything else here.
An import workflow is created automatically when a STORAGE ROUTE is
created, named after it and pointed at it (app.py
_create_import_workflow_for_route). Seeding one here as well produced a
workflow with no source that could not run until someone connected it
by hand - the step this removed.
The entry stays: its name, type and description are what the
route-created workflow is built from, and is_ingestion_script() and the
trigger chain both resolve through it.

workflows.name: Import Files
workflows.description: The same import - same dates, same duplicate checks, same catalog - scheduled for speed: reads each file once, with as many streams as the storage suits (one or two on a spinning disk), shows photos as they arrive, and renders previews in the background.
_default_comment: Not seeded, like the phased import above. THE DEFAULT since 2026-09-27:
every new storage route's import workflow runs this script
(app.py DEFAULT_INGEST_SCRIPT). AIRLOCK_INGEST_SCRIPT=
io_picture_import_workflow.py gives new routes the phased one again.
See documentation/features/ingestion-architecture.md.

workflows.name: Create Events
workflows.description: Group photos into events by capture time and location.

workflows.name: Extract Locations
workflows.description: Group GPS coordinates into places by proximity, for review.

workflows.name: Resolve Locations
workflows.description: Record where each photo was and what place that is, including places inherited from an event.

workflows.name: Find Faces
workflows.description: Look through imported photographs for faces and save a crop of each one. Finds faces; does not say who they are.

workflows.name: Measure Faces
workflows.description: Turn each face crop into the numbers the matching steps compare. Nothing can be recognised until this has run. Resumable: stopping loses at most the crop in flight.
_comment: Order 35: after Auto Detect Faces (30), which creates the crops, and
before Face Recognition (50), which needs their vectors.
Its own workflow because embedding used to be a side effect of
scoring - so it only advanced while somebody tolerated a full
catalog scoring run, and its cost landed on whoever tagged a face.

workflows.name: Learn Tagged Faces
workflows.description: Take the faces you have named by hand and make them the examples everything else is matched against.

workflows.name: Match Faces by Appearance
workflows.description: Compare every unnamed face with the faces you have named, and record how close each one is. Suggests; never names anybody by itself.

workflows.name: Re-rank Matches by Context
workflows.description: Re-order the suggestions using who appears with whom, when the photographs were taken and which event they belong to. Looks at no images; only at what the steps above already found.

workflows.name: Measure and Match Pets
workflows.description: Crop each detected animal, measure it, and compare it with the pets you have named.
_default_comment: NOT seeded with a new catalog. The `workflows` table has no `enabled`
column, so EXISTENCE IS THE SWITCH: these two rows are created when
pets are switched on in the catalog form (POST /catalogs or PUT
/catalogs/<id>), by app.apply_pets_enabled through
workflow_defaults.create_pet_workflows, exactly as a storage route
creates its import workflow.
A household with no pets therefore has no pet workflow rows at all -
nothing to run, nothing queued, nothing to explain. The entry stays here
because this file is where a workflow's name, type and description live,
and create_pet_workflows reads them from it rather than keeping a second
copy that would drift.
See documentation/specs/pet-recognition-spec.md section 10.

workflows.name: Group Unnamed Pets
workflows.description: Group animals that look like the same one, ready for you to name them in a single step.
_default_comment: Not seeded, for the same reason as Identify Pets above.
Groups are NOT pets: no `people` row exists for an unnamed animal. Naming
a group is what creates one, and that single action also writes person_id
to every member detection - which is what turns hundreds of photographs
into 'photos with Rex' without anybody tagging them by hand.
